key_insight: ShortCoder combines external knowledge augmentation with syntax-aware code representations to generate semantically equivalent code using far fewer tokens, cutting inference cost without sacrificing correctness.
problem_solved: Large language models for code require one full model pass per generated token and must hold long contexts in memory, leading to high latency, compute, and memory overhead for code generation; ShortCoder addresses this token inefficiency.
method: Knowledge-augmented retrieval: fetch relevant APIs, examples, and templates to prefill or constrain generation and reduce redundant token output.
Syntax-aware compression/optimization: transform code into compact, grammar-preserving representations (e.g., macros, structured tokens, AST-based encodings) that require fewer tokens to express.
Decoder integration: map optimized representations back to executable source during or after LLM decoding so the model generates shorter sequences while preserving semantics.
impact: Lower token counts translate to fewer inference passes, reduced latency and cost, and smaller memory footprints—making large-code LLMs more practical for production, edge, and hardware-constrained deployments.

paper_title: ShortCoder: Knowledge-Augmented Syntax Optimization for Token-Efficient Code Generation
